gaps: Borrowed mouth makes answerability depend on an arrangement of people, not only on available evidence. The sealed-mouth residue asks whether the habitat of an answer must change first; this produced the changed question for breath two.
accepted: Threshold foundling: “Is the river clean?” becomes “Which harms may count as clean?”; an answer must expose and justify the tolerated injury hidden inside the requested fact.

Defect organ: “Why does the bell crack?” becomes “What can its crack detect?”; an answer must demonstrate a usable discrimination produced by the supposed fault, not merely redescribe damage as a gift.

Specimen molt: “Why did this bell crack?” becomes “Which bells must crack under these conditions?”; an answer must delimit a class and its exceptions, not furnish a more detailed biography of one object.

Knife in the cause: “What made the bell crack?” becomes “Which reachable change would prevent the next crack?”; an answer must identify an effective intervention, even if the fullest explanation names causes nobody can alter.

Contour of ignorance: “Where is the lost chamber?” becomes “Which locations can the surviving traces still distinguish?”; an answer must draw the boundary between recoverable and irrecoverable differences, rather than choose a location inside an evidential tie.

Twin tribunal: “Which account is right?” becomes “What occurrence would make the accounts disagree?”; an answer must construct a discriminating encounter, not add support that both accounts can absorb.

Debt in the units: “How much birdsong is one new road worth?” becomes “Can these losses enter the same arithmetic?”; an answer must justify a conversion or delimit where conversion fails, before calculating a balance.

Borrowed mouth: “What does the village want?” becomes “Who may answer as the village, and who may refuse that voice?”; an answer must establish a defensible speaking arrangement, not average the replies already easiest to collect.

residue.item: Magnifying glass: ask the same question in finer detail.
residue.why: Rejected: increased resolution can leave the criterion for a successful answer unchanged; it is not itself a species change.

residue.item: The sealed mouth: a question becomes a place where an answer can survive.
residue.why: Held as residue: survival might mean safety for a witness, durability of a record, or continuity of a language. The image is fertile but does not yet specify what the new answer owes.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or exhaustive partition; one episode may undergo several transformations.
The seriation orders loci of change, not difficulty, value, or historical development. Map edges are conditional authored claims.
Last translator depends on an invented continuity of concern across a species change; the wild probe investigates that premise instead of asserting it.
The unresolved orphan-answer seed remains outside the final list because the live-question requirement has not yet been met.

gaps: The sealed-mouth image separated into survivable testimony, preservation of a measured subject, and protected warrant; these require different kinds of answer. Last translator then removes the tacit constant shared by all three: an asker who remains able to recognize success.
accepted: Unborn witness: “Which account is right?” becomes “What must first be built so their difference can leave a trace?”; an answer must bring a discriminating instrument or setting into existence, not name evidence the present world cannot produce.

Harbor before testimony: “What happened in that house?” becomes “Under what conditions could its inhabitants tell us without punishment?”; an answer must make truthful speech survivable, rather than interpret silence as missing information.

Answer as wound: “What is inside the sealed seed?” becomes “What can we learn while leaving it able to germinate?”; an answer must meet a preservation constraint, or openly show that the desired knowledge and the living subject cannot both be retained.

Forecast with teeth: “What will the crowd do?” becomes “What announced forecast remains defensible after the crowd hears it?”; an answer must account for its own circulation as a cause, rather than predict a world in which nobody receives it.

Chorus without unison: “Which account of the border is correct?” becomes “What joint account can preserve incompatible lived borders without pretending they coincide?”; an answer must specify how situated accounts coexist and where they cannot be combined, not elect a single victorious viewpoint.

Question sanctuary: “What is the hidden name?” becomes “How can a claim be settled without making that name obtainable?”; an answer must establish a protected route to sufficient warrant, or demonstrate its impossibility, rather than treat maximal disclosure as success.

Continuing answer: “Has the estrangement ended?” becomes “What recurring practice would keep an answer of yes true?”; an answer must become a renewable pattern of repair with recognizable lapses, not a verdict whose truth is allowed to expire unnoticed.

Last translator: in an invented world where understanding an answer changes one’s species, “What are they telling me?” becomes “Which transformation lets me understand while preserving the concern that made me ask?”; an answer must carry a recognizable question across the loss of its original asker, not merely transmit a proposition.

residue.item: Perfect refusal: every dangerous question is answered by silence.
residue.why: Rejected: silence need not settle anything and erases the distinction between protecting a witness, preserving a subject, and proving a claim without disclosure.

residue.item: Orphan answer: a civilization leaves an answer whose originating question no surviving mind can ask.
residue.why: Unresolved seed: wonderfully displaced, but currently it transforms the interpreter’s task rather than a live question. It needs a continuity criterion before admission.

neighbors.left: Twin tribunal: “Which account is right?” becomes “What occurrence would make the accounts disagree?”; an answer must construct a discriminating encounter, not add support that both accounts can absorb.
neighbors.right: Unborn witness: “Which account is right?” becomes “What must first be built so their difference can leave a trace?”; an answer must bring a discriminating instrument or setting into existence, not name evidence the present world cannot produce.
neighbors.separating_case: Two theories predict different colors from the same available reagent: Twin tribunal is satisfied by specifying that trial. If they instead predict a phase difference no existing detector resolves, identifying the difference is not enough for Unborn witness; an answer owes a workable means of making it observable.

checks.boundary_case: “Why did this bell crack?” → “Why did this bronze bell crack last Tuesday?” is not admitted merely for added detail: an adequate causal explanation could satisfy both. A change in wording is insufficient without a changed obligation.
checks.form_inference: The map forks Borrowed mouth into plural representation and safety: adding legitimate speakers can fail in either dimension independently. Its Chorus → Borrowed mouth return shows that an answer can expose a missing answerer and reopen its own authority. The line cannot express this revisable loop; late placement does not mean final settlement.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each admitted item names a new burden of answerhood; the invented-world endpoint retains the strange continuity problem rather than replacing it with ordinary translation advice.
